detailed_analysis: The spectrum is identified as OLIVINE on the basis of the full band pattern, per the mandatory trap-disambiguation rule for single-region-820-880 features. The decisive evidence is the RESOLVED PAIR at 822.11 +/- 0.02 and 853.87 +/- 0.02 cm-1 (separation 31.75 cm-1), accompanied by weak companion bands at 917.83 +/- 0.10 and 959.62 +/- 0.19 cm-1 and a suite of weak SiO4 bending/lattice modes at 221.6, 300.9, 325.2, 368.8, 428.1, 540.9, 584.8, 606.5 cm-1. This rules out competing single-strong-band candidates: uranyl (single symmetric band, no doublet, no 918/960), scheelite/wolframite tungstates (would lack 918/960 companions and add 320-400 bending unlike this pattern), and apatite (whose dominant band is a single ~964 nu1, here only a weak feature). The doublet positions 822/854 map onto forsterite-rich olivine (Fo endmember reference ~824/856 cm-1). The measured centers sit ~2 cm-1 below the pure-Fo reference, and the doublet separation and DB1 position are consistent with a Mg-rich composition with minor Fe (Fo roughly 80-90); precise Fo# would require calibrated peak-position vs composition curves. The fit quality (R2=0.996, RMSE=56 counts) is high, and the doublet parameters are exceptionally well constrained (center errors ~0.02 cm-1, FWHM errors <0.1 cm-1). However, the localized structured residual on the strong bands indicates genuine band asymmetry / Lorentzian-wing over-projection into the 716-790 region; an asymmetric or split-pseudo-Voigt profile for the two strong bands would likely remove this and slightly revise their widths. Weak-band eta values pin to 0 or 1 with large errors, so their Gaussian/Lorentzian character is undetermined and their areas carry 10-25% uncertainty. No chemistry (EDX/XRF) was supplied, so the assignment is pattern-only but strongly self-consistent across positions AND relative intensities.

scientific_claims.claim: The spectrum shows a resolved Si-O stretch doublet at 822.11 +/- 0.02 and 853.87 +/- 0.02 cm-1 (separation 31.75 cm-1) with weak 917.8 +/- 0.1 and 959.6 +/- 0.2 cm-1 companions, diagnostic of forsterite-rich (Mg-dominant) olivine.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: The doublet position and separation are compositional indicators (Fo#) for olivine, enabling non-destructive mineral identification and Mg/Fe estimation relevant to petrology and planetary/meteoritic sample characterization.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone calibrated the olivine DB1/DB2 Raman doublet positions (~822/854 cm-1) against Fo# to quantify Mg/Fe content in unknown silicate samples?

model_type: Sum of 12 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a flat linear baseline (Levenberg-Marquardt / TRF least squares). Band centers (cm-1): ~220, ~305, ~325, ~370, ~428, ~542, ~590, ~610, ~822 (strong), ~854 (strong), ~918, ~960. The 810-870 region is treated as a RESOLVED DOUBLET (two symmetric components at ~822 and ~854), not one asymmetric band. Each component: amp*[eta*Lorentzian + (1-eta)*Gaussian], independent center, FWHM, amplitude, eta. Baseline: linear (near-zero) fitted as a model parameter. Constraints: amp>=0, FWHM in (1,60), eta in [0,1], centers within +-10 cm-1 of seeds. Background assessment: rolling-minimum baseline area fraction = 0.276 (<<0.40) => NOT fluorescence-dominated, no ALS applied per plan step 1. Cosmic single-pixel spikes removed via median filter.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 12 pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat/linear baseline. Band centers (initial): ~220, ~305, ~325, ~370, ~428, ~542, ~590/610 (one band ~590 with weak shoulder ~610), ~822 (strong), ~854 (strong), ~918, ~960 cm⁻¹. Each component: I·[η·Lorentzian + (1−η)·Gaussian] with independent center, width, amplitude, and mixing fraction η. Baseline: constant offset (near zero) — use linear baseline to absorb minor slope.

issues.problem: Fit sits systematically ABOVE near-zero data (over-projection up to ~200 counts); the heavily-Lorentzian pseudo-Voigt wing of the 822 band extends intensity into a region that is genuinely empty in the data.
Oscillatory residual (~300 counts) on the strong peaks.
